subproblems.title: The chosen approximate tangent plane equals any approximate tangent plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, x ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P. If Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), with η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) and H^n = μHE[n]), then approxTangentPlane n M x = Q, where approxTangentPlane n M x is the contract's choice: a chosen plane Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' if such a plane exists, and ⊥ otherwise.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → approxTangentPlane n M x = Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dpf_itt_approxTangentPlane_eq of DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.image_tangent_transport-a1.chosen_tangent_plane-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 34325ececca5ed226212e37aa67e711a3a090e9d). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above (checked against dag.json and against the declaration in that commit), so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: supplied step 3 (the good set G). At μ-a.e. x ∈ M, R.orients gives Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x; this child gives approxTangentPlane n M x = Q_x, so the hypothesis (approxTangentPlane n M x).starProjection v = v (v ∈ L) becomes Q_x.starProjection v = v, i.e. L ≤ Q_x (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). This is the supplied sentence 'approxTangentPlane n M x = Q_x by uniqueness, and starProjection_eq_self_iff'. In the accepted proof below, phrases such as 'the parent proof' and its step numbers refer to the reused node's original parent, not to the selected node.

Accepted proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (the identification Q(F_i b) = range DF_i(b) by Exists.choose_spec and uniqueness), i.e. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1) (uniqueness of the approximate tangent space), applied to the contract's choice function. No hypothesis on M, x, n or P is used.
1. Definition. In GMT/Ch07/Contract.lean, approxTangentPlane n M x is defined (classically) as h.choose if h : ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q' holds, and as ⊥ otherwise.
2. The condition holds. From hQ : HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q we get h := ⟨Q, hQ⟩ : ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q'. Unfolding approxTangentPlane and taking the positive branch of the dependent if-then-else (rw [dite_eq_left h]; dite_eq_left is the current name of the deprecated dif_pos) gives approxTangentPlane n M x = h.choose.
3. The chosen plane is an approximate tangent plane. By Exists.choose_spec, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x h.choose.
4. Uniqueness. SimonGMT's Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1)) states: if HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₁ and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q₂, then Q₁ = Q₂. (Its proof: the limits ∫_{Q₁} f dH^n and ∫_{Q₂} f dH^n of the same net coincide for every f ∈ C_c, so H^n⌞Q₁ = H^n⌞Q₂ as regular measures, and the support of H^n⌞Q_k is Q_k because finrank Q_k = n.) It needs no further hypotheses on Euclid P. Applied to step 3 and hQ it gives h.choose = Q.
5. By steps 2 and 4, approxTangentPlane n M x = Q.
proof_key_steps: The hypothesis provides the witness ⟨Q, hQ⟩ of the existential in approxTangentPlane, so the definition returns the chosen plane h.choose.
Exists.choose_spec: h.choose is an approximate tangent plane of M at x.
HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (Simon 3.1.5(1)) identifies h.choose with Q.

subproblems.title: An n-covector on vectors spanned by an orthonormal n-frame is det(⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩) times its value on the frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) (indexed by Fin n) be an orthonormal family in ℝᴾ = Euclid P and let b = (b₁, …, bₙ) be a family in ℝᴾ with bⱼ ∈ span{τ₁, …, τₙ} for every j. Then for every n-covector α of ℝᴾ (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form), α(b₁, …, bₙ) = det(𝒜)·α(τ₁, …, τₙ), where 𝒜 is the n×n real matrix 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ b : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, b j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α b = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).det * α τ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.graph_cycle_regular-a1.graph_orientation_jacobian-a1.covector_frame_det-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 73310ec921452a01670f397b34d1cf3cd7135598). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above (checked against dag.json and against the declaration in that commit), so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: supplied step 3 (structure at x ∈ G). Let τ be the orthonormal frame of Q_x with ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ), g an orthonormal basis of Q_x ∩ L^⊥ and b := (f_1, …, f_d, g_1, …, g_m) (Lean: Fin.append f g ∘ Fin.cast (Nat.add_sub_of_le hd.le).symm), an orthonormal frame spanning Q_x. Applied to (τ, b) and to (b, τ), this child gives α(b) = D·α(τ) and α(τ) = D·α(b) for every n-covector α, with D = det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩) = det(⟨b_i, τ_j⟩) (transpose). This is the supplied 'τ = O(f, g) with O orthogonal and α(τ) = det(O)α(f, g)'. In the accepted proof below, phrases such as 'the parent proof' and its step numbers refer to the reused node's original parent, not to the selected node.

Accepted proof:
Source: step 3(i) of the parent proof (the restriction α_L of α to L is a multiple of the basis determinant of L, evaluated at b), stated for an arbitrary orthonormal frame τ of the subspace L = span(range τ) containing b.
Notation: ℝᵐ means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); ⟨x, y⟩ is inner ℝ x y; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝⁿ; an n-covector of ℝᴾ is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ (a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝᴾ × ⋯ × ℝᴾ → ℝ); MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors); for a continuous linear map F, F* = F.adjoint and det of an endomorphism is ContinuousLinearMap.det (= LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map). L := span ℝ (range τ) ⊆ ℝᴾ, an n-family c in L has underlying ambient family ↑c.
1. A basis of L indexed by Fin n. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of its span: e := Module.Basis.span hτ.linearIndependent is a basis (e₁, …, eₙ) of L whose underlying vectors are ↑eᵢ = τᵢ (Module.Basis.span_apply).
2. Restriction of α to L. Let α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype, i.e. α_L(c₁, …, cₙ) := α(↑c₁, …, ↑cₙ) for cᵢ ∈ L; it is an alternating n-linear form on L. Put b'ⱼ := ⟨bⱼ, hbⱼ⟩ ∈ L (hypothesis). Then α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α(↑e) = α_L(e) (both by unfolding, using ↑eᵢ = τᵢ).
3. Alternating n-forms on the n-dimensional space L with basis e are multiples of the basis determinant: α_L = α_L(e) • det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b').
4. The coordinate matrix. det_e(b') = det M with Mᵢⱼ := e.repr(b'ⱼ)ᵢ (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply). We claim Mᵢⱼ = ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩. Indeed b'ⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ • eₗ (Module.Basis.sum_repr); taking underlying vectors (Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul) gives bⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ • τₗ, and taking the inner product with τᵢ and using orthonormality, ⟨τᵢ, Σₗ Mₗⱼ τₗ⟩ = Mᵢⱼ (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Hence M = 𝒜.
5. Combining steps 2–4: α(b) = α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b') = α(τ)·det 𝒜 = det(𝒜)·α(τ). ∎
(The argument is uniform in n; for n = 0 both sides reduce to α of the empty family, det of the empty matrix being 1.)
(The accepted kernel-checked Lean proof of this exact type is the declaration Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span at commit 73310ec921452a01670f397b34d1cf3cd7135598.)
proof_key_steps: τ orthonormal ⇒ linearly independent ⇒ basis e := Module.Basis.span of L = span(range τ) with ↑eᵢ = τᵢ.
Restrict α to L: α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype; α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α_L(e).
AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det: α_L = α_L(e)·det_e, so α(b) = α(τ)·det_e(b').
det_e(b') = det of the coordinate matrix, whose (i,j) entry is ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ by expanding bⱼ = Σₗ cₗ τₗ and orthonormality.
Hence α(b) = det(⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩)·α(τ).

subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same plane both take absolute value 1 on a common covector
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P, and let ξ_1, ξ_2 ∈ MultiVector P n both be unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_k Q for k = 1, 2: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' spanning Q and signs with ξ_1(α) = ±α(τ) and ξ_2(α) = ±α(τ') for every n-covector α). Then there is an n-covector α on ℝ^P (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n) with |ξ_1(α)| = 1 and |ξ_2(α)| = 1. (With ξ_1 = ξ_2 this shows that a unit orientation is non-zero.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ₁ ξ₂ : MultiVector P n), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₁ Q → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ₂ Q → ∃ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ₁ α| = 1 ∧ |ξ₂ α| = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.unit_orientations_common_unit_covector of DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.imrep_measure_unique-a1.orientation_common_covector-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit deb99356ba22fa0a7c3b91feabd427b84a2fb40d). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above (checked against dag.json and against the declaration in that commit), so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: supplied step 3 (the sign ε = ±1). Applied with ξ_1 = ξ_2 = ξ(x) (a unit orientation of Q_x), it gives a covector α_0 with |ξ(x)(α_0)| = 1, hence α_0(τ) ≠ 0. With the two identities from the sibling covector_frame_det, α_0(τ) = D·α_0(b) = D²·α_0(τ), so (D² − 1)·α_0(τ) = 0 and D = ±1; therefore ξ(x)(α) = ±α(τ) = ε·α(f, g) with ε ∈ {1, −1}. This realizes the supplied 'τ = O(f, g) with O orthogonal … ξ(x)(α) = εα(f, g) for all α, with ε = ±1'. In the accepted proof below, phrases such as 'the parent proof' and its step numbers refer to the reused node's original parent, not to the selected node.

Accepted proof:
Source: steps 1(b) and 1(d) of the parent proof of representation independence of θH^n⌞M (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3)): the frame-determinant covector δ_τ(w) = det(⟨τ_i, w_j⟩)_{i,j} satisfies δ_τ(τ) = 1 and, for any orthonormal τ' with the same span, δ_τ(τ') = det O ∈ {−1, +1} with O = (⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩); hence a unit orientation built on τ or on τ' takes the value ±1 at δ_τ.

1. Unpack the hypotheses: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(τ) = Q = span(τ') and signs ε_1, ε_2 ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ_1(α) = ε_1·α(τ) and ξ_2(α) = ε_2·α(τ') for every n-covector α.
2. (The frame-determinant covector.) For w = (w_1,…,w_n) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n put δ(w) := det(⟨τ_i, w_j⟩)_{i,j=1}^n. It is n-linear (the determinant is linear in each column, and the j-th column (⟨τ_i, w_j⟩)_i depends linearly on w_j alone) and alternating (if w_j = w_k for some j ≠ k the matrix has two equal columns, so δ(w) = 0). It is continuous: by the Leibniz formula and Cauchy–Schwarz with ‖τ_i‖ = 1, |δ(w)| ≤ Σ_σ ∏_j |⟨τ_{σ(j)}, w_j⟩| ≤ n!·∏_j ‖w_j‖, and a multilinear map satisfying such a bound is continuous. Hence δ is an n-covector on ℝ^P. (For n = 0, δ is the constant 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.)
3. δ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = det(I_n) = 1, by orthonormality of τ.
4. Put O_{ij} := ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩, so δ(τ') = det O. Each τ'_j lies in Q = span(τ); writing τ'_j = Σ_i c_i τ_i and pairing with τ_k gives c_k = ⟨τ_k, τ'_j⟩ = O_{kj}, i.e. τ'_j = Σ_i O_{ij} τ_i. Therefore ⟨τ'_j, τ'_k⟩ = Σ_i O_{ij} O_{ik} = (OᵀO)_{jk}. Since τ' is orthonormal, OᵀO = I_n, so (det O)² = det(Oᵀ)·det(O) = det(OᵀO) = 1 and det O ∈ {1, −1}.
5. Take α := δ. Then |ξ_1(δ)| = |ε_1|·|δ(τ)| = 1 by step 3 and |ξ_2(δ)| = |ε_2|·|det O| = 1 by step 4. ∎
(The accepted kernel-checked Lean proof of this exact type, which realizes δ as det_b ∘ π_Q made continuous by AlternatingMap.mkContinuous, is the declaration Submission.unit_orientations_common_unit_covector at commit deb99356ba22fa0a7c3b91feabd427b84a2fb40d.)
proof_key_steps: Unpack: ξ_1(α) = ε_1α(τ), ξ_2(α) = ε_2α(τ') with τ, τ' orthonormal frames of Q and ε_k = ±1.
The frame determinant δ(w) = det(⟨τ_i, w_j⟩) is a continuous alternating n-form with δ(τ) = 1.
O = (⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩) satisfies OᵀO = I because τ'_j = Σ_i O_{ij}τ_i, so δ(τ') = det O = ±1.
Hence |ξ_1(δ)| = |ξ_2(δ)| = 1; take α = δ.

subproblems.title: The space of n-covectors on ℝ^P is finite-dimensional
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers P and n, the real vector space Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ, with its pointwise ℝ-module structure, is finite-dimensional over ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lcn_covector_finiteDimensional of DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.support_null-a1.local_carrier_null-a1.covector_finite_dimensional-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 127487dd6bed94a74811cb8523d5535db984c906). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above (checked against dag.json and against the declaration in that commit), so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: (i) supplied steps 6–7: for the Borel data map Γ(z) = (1_M(z)θ(z), 1_M(z)θ(z)ξ̃(z)) (its components are measurable, resp. strongly measurable, without this child), the comparison sets B = {(v, x) : x ∈ M, Γ(x + v) ≠ Γ(x)}, B' and their slices are Borel. With a basis (β_i) of the finite-dimensional Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n (Module.finBasis), two n-vectors are equal iff they agree on every β_i, so {a : Γ(φ a) ≠ Γ(ψ a)} is the complement of a finite intersection of sets {u = u'} of real Borel functions (measurableSet_eq_fun). After `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`, MultiVector P n has no MetrizableSpace, ContinuousSub or SecondCountableTopology instance (probed), so this is how the supplied 'B and B' are Borel' claim is realized. (ii) supplied step 1: ♭ is linear on the finite-dimensional space Λ^n, hence continuous linear (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap), which makes y ↦ ♭(ω(t + y)) a test m-form. In the accepted proof below, phrases such as 'the parent proof' and its step numbers refer to the reused node's original parent, not to the selected node.

Accepted proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof. Finite-dimensionality of Λ^n is used in step 8 to test ξ(x) against a finite basis. Mathlib provides no FiniteDimensional instance for continuous alternating maps, so the fact is proved directly.
Notation. Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n = (ℝ^P)[⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ. For α ∈ Λ^n and w : Fin n → ℝ^P write α(w) = α(w_1, …, w_n). Addition and scalar multiplication on Λ^n are pointwise.
1. Standard basis. Let e = (e_1, …, e_P) be the standard basis of ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), for instance the Module.Basis underlying the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ.
2. The evaluation map. For each multi-index I : Fin n → Fin P put e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}). Define Φ : Λ^n → ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)} by Φ(α)(I) := α(e_I). Because the operations on Λ^n are pointwise, Φ(α + β)(I) = α(e_I) + β(e_I) and Φ(c·α)(I) = c·α(e_I). So Φ is ℝ-linear.
3. Φ is injective. Let α, β ∈ Λ^n with Φ(α) = Φ(β).
- Then α(e_v) = β(e_v) for every v : Fin n → Fin P, in particular for every injective v.
- The underlying algebraic alternating maps of α and β are multilinear and alternating. Two such maps that agree on every tuple (e_{v(1)}, …, e_{v(n)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating). So the underlying alternating maps of α and β coincide.
- A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). Hence α = β.
4. Conclusion. The index set Fin n → Fin P is finite (P^n elements). So the codomain ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)} is a finite product of copies of ℝ and is finite-dimensional. A vector space with an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective). By steps 2 and 3, FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n) holds.
proof_key_steps: Define the linear evaluation map Φ : Λ^n → ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)}, Φ(α)(I) = α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}), on standard-basis tuples.
Φ is injective: alternating maps that agree on basis tuples are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating), and toAlternatingMap is injective.
The codomain is finite-dimensional, so FiniteDimensional.of_injective gives FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n).

subproblems.title: Integrability and sup-norm estimate for the IMRep pairing with a bounded, compactly supported covector field
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep U n, C ⊆ U compact and B ∈ ℝ. Let F : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) be a.e. strongly measurable for μ := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), with F(x) = 0 for all x ∉ C and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. Then x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-integrable, and |∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(F(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ B · (∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U C : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (F : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (B : ℝ), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → AEStronglyMeasurable F (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) → (∀ x, x ∉ C → F x = 0) → (∀ x, ‖F x‖ ≤ B) → Integrable (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x)) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) ∧ |∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x) ∂μHE[n]| ≤ B * (∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ C, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n]).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le of DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.pairing_bound-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 5c8c6597411e77948b224fda014774beaa21ebaf). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above (checked against dag.json and against the declaration in that commit), so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: supplied step 5 (action formula). With U = ℝ^P, F = ω (a test n-form; a.e. strongly measurable since continuous), C = tsupport ω (compact) and B = sup_x ‖ω(x)‖ < ∞, it gives integrability of x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) for H^n⌞M. By step 3b this function equals h = θζ(♭ω) H^n⌞M-a.e., so ∫_M h^± dH^n < ∞ and (C1) of spine_coarea applies to h⁺ and h⁻ (the supplied '|h| ≤ θ‖ω‖_∞1_{tsupport ω} … finite integrals'). In the accepted proof below, phrases such as 'the parent proof' and its step numbers refer to the reused node's original parent, not to the selected node.

Accepted proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the parent proof, together with the estimate in its step 6. Simon 6.2.24(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 414–425) says that when M_W(T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, f_#T(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), df_x#ξ(x)⟩θ dHⁿ makes sense for C¹ f. The printed text leaves the integrability and the estimate to the reader; they are supplied here. This proof uses the sibling theorem orient_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le).
Notation:
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M;
- h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)), with θ(x) viewed in ℝ;
- 1_C θ := C.indicator (fun y => (θ y : ℝ)) and g(x) := B·(1_C θ)(x).
0. (orient_bound, made explicit.) For μ-a.e. x and every n-covector β, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm). Indeed, by R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) and a sign with ξ(x)(β) = β(τ) for all β or ξ(x)(β) = −β(τ) for all β (IsUnitOrientationOf); then |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ ‖β‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the product is 1 since ‖τ_i‖ = 1, and empty when n = 0). In the reused node this is its accepted sibling Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.orient_bound-a1, candidate 056f1b9b0f63f29ad638c335a0b984ac1606c017), cited below as orient_bound.
1. C is measurable. C is compact, hence closed (IsCompact.isClosed), hence a Borel, i.e. measurable, set.
2. θ is measurable. θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable (R.measurable_mult), and every function on ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat). So x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
3. Restriction identity. Since C is measurable, μ.restrict C = (μHE[n].restrict M).restrict C = μHE[n].restrict (C ∩ M) = μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C) (Measure.restrict_restrict, inter_comm).
4. 1_C θ and g are μ-integrable.
   - By R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set C ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] ≠ ∞.
   - Since θ(x) ≥ 0, its extended norm ‖(θ(x) : ℝ)‖ₑ equals (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) (Real.enorm_natCast). By step 3, ∫⁻ ‖θ‖ₑ d(μ.restrict C) = ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] < ∞.
   - With step 2, θ is integrable on C with respect to μ (IntegrableOn).
   - Hence 1_C θ is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, C measurable), and so is g = B·1_C θ (Integrable.const_mul).
5. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
   - The evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) from MultiVector P n × Covector (Euclid P) n to ℝ is continuous, since ζ ranges over continuous linear maps (continuous_fst.clm_apply continuous_snd).
   - ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), and so is F (hypothesis). So x ↦ ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
   - Multiplying by the measurable θ of step 2 preserves this (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).
6. Domination |h| ≤ g μ-a.e. By orient_bound, for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all n-covectors β. Fix such an x.
   - If x ∈ C, then (1_C θ)(x) = θ(x). Using θ(x) ≥ 0 and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B: |h(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(F(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖F(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·B = g(x).
   - If x ∉ C, then F(x) = 0 by hypothesis, so ξ(x)(F(x)) = 0 (ξ(x) is linear) and |h(x)| = 0. Also g(x) = B·0 = 0.
   Hence ‖h(x)‖ ≤ g(x) for μ-a.e. x.
7. Integrability. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (step 5) and dominated μ-a.e. by the μ-integrable g (steps 4 and 6). So h is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono'). This is the first conjunct.
8. Value of ∫ g dμ:
   ∫ g dμ = B·∫ 1_C θ dμ (integral_const_mul)
   = B·∫ θ d(μ.restrict C) (integral_indicator, C measurable)
   = B·∫ θ d(μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C)) (step 3)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} ENNReal.ofReal(θ) dμHE[n]).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; θ ≥ 0 and is a.e. strongly measurable)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast).
9. Estimate. By definition of the set integral, ∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n] = ∫ h dμ. Then |∫ h dμ| = ‖∫ h dμ‖ ≤ ∫ g dμ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, using integrability of g and step 6). By step 8 this gives |∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n]| ≤ B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal, the second conjunct.
proof_key_steps: orient_bound: a.e. on M, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ because ξ(x) = ±(evaluation at an orthonormal frame).
C compact ⇒ measurable; θ measurable; μ.restrict C = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ C).
Local integrability of θ on the compact C ⊆ U makes g = B·1_C θ μ-integrable.
h = θ·ξ(F) is a.e. strongly measurable via continuity of evaluation.
orient_bound together with F = 0 off C and ‖F‖ ≤ B gives |h| ≤ g μ-a.e.
Integrable.mono' gives integrability; |∫ h| ≤ ∫ g = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ).toReal.
